newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah lower, overnight money volatile.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah lower, overnight money volatile.

text.p: Indonesia's rupiah was lower against the dollar in late trading on Tuesday, dealers said.
Overnight money was volatile, soaring to a high of 17 percent from 12.0 percent before settling at seven percent.
Some dealers said the weakening of the rupiah could be due to late excess rupiah supply while some said sentiment on the dollar has been bullish since the morning.
"I don't know of any rumours. But offshores kept buying, driving the dollar higher and higher in a relatively thin market in the afternoon," one European bank dealer said.
One local bank dealer said it was possible that offshore players were covering short positions or going long on dollars ahead of the approaching general elections on May 29.
"Some people are feeling uncomfortable (about the elections). They are moving to cover first which is also reflected by a light uptrend in longer-term swap rates," the dealer said.

"The tone remains biddish on the dollar," the European bank dealer said, adding that there was also speculation the rupiah market might be tight on Wednesday. He said operators remained sensitive about liquidity following Monday's volatility.
Spot rupiah fell to 2,418.0/19.0 at 0845 GMT from an opening of 2,414.5/15.5. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,416.6/17.1 and 2,415.0/15.5, respectively.
One Japanese bank dealer said the dollar was on an uptrend after the central bank depreciated the rupiah by one point.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band to 2,403/2,595 and the conversion band at 2,403/2,451 on Tuesday.
One-month swaps increased to 11.1/11.5 from 10.75/11.50 and two to 22.0/22.5 from 21.75/23.0. Three- and six-month swaps were stable at 33.50/34.25 and 69.75/70.75, respectively.
